Monotonicity of each amplitude quotient reduces all possible positive prime two-cycles to one strictly increasing scalar function with explicitly computed endpoint limits. Those limits prove exactly zero versus exactly one orbit at the sharp inequality, including equality and endpoints. Exponentiating both amplitude equations reconstructs both map arrows; a direct Jacobian computation verifies the flip-factor equivalence. The parameter assumptions and boundaries are explicit; finite examples are corroborative only.

value.rationale: In a two-species competitive Ricker map with known in-phase and antiphase multistability elsewhere, a complete positive prime-period-two orbit count is a natural nonlinear dynamics question. The sharp determinant boundary simultaneously proves the existence or total absence of positive two-cycles and uniqueness wherever one exists; its global consequence and rigorous forced phase agreement cannot be obtained from linearization or finite orbit plots alone. The result is useful for delineating possible coexistence oscillations while making no unsupported attraction or higher-period claims.
